adds.title: Pernambuco foi o segundo estado que mais matou pessoas trans e travestis em 2025, diz estudo
adds.summary: Diario de Pernambuco, Jan. 27, 2026: Pernambuco was the second Brazilian state with the most killings of trans and travesti people in 2025, with 7 homicides, per the ANTRA dossier released on Jan. 26 — the state's lowest annual count since 2022 (13), after 9 in 2023 and 8 in 2024. The dossier counts 80 trans people killed nationally in 2025, 349 killings across the Northeast from 2017 to 2025, and 83 violent deaths of trans people in Pernambuco over six years, 6th-most in the national ranking for that period. For this record: a Pernambuco-specific confirmation of the state's 2025 total and a year-by-year series showing its repeated high ranking.

adds.title: Mulher trans é morta a tiros em Belo Jardim
adds.summary: G1 Caruaru e Região, Oct. 3, 2025: a trans woman was shot dead inside her home on Oct. 2, 2025 in Belo Jardim, in the Agreste interior of Pernambuco, and the Civil Police opened an inquiry to identify the author and motive, with no arrests reported at publication. The report recalls the national ANTRA count of 122 trans people killed in Brazil in 2024. For this record: a documented 2025 killing outside the Recife capital region, consistent with the dossier finding that most such killings occur in interior municipalities.

adds.title: Morte de transexual negra é registrada no Agreste de Pernambuco; mais um caso preocupa ativistas
adds.summary: Alma Preta, July 7, 2021: Fabiana da Silva Lucas, a 30-year-old Black trans woman, was found dead on the morning of that day along highway PE-160 in Santa Cruz do Capibaribe, in the Agreste of Pernambuco, killed by several knife strikes; it was the state's third recorded case of killed trans or travesti people that month. Pernambuco's Civil Police told press the suspect, a 22-year-old known as 'Gaúcho', was lynched by locals at the scene. For this record: a documented interior-state killing of a Black travesti matching the victim profile and geography described in the summary.

adds.title: Morte de mulher trans na Bahia é investigada como feminicídio; suspeito deixou corpo em delegacia e foi liberado
adds.summary: G1 Bahia, Dec. 9, 2025: police are investigating as feminicide the killing of Rhianna, an 18-year-old trans woman, choked to death in Luís Eduardo Magalhães, in the west of Bahia, on the weekend of Dec. 6-7. The suspect, a 19-year-old app driver, drove the victim's body to the police station himself and was released after confessing and claiming self-defence; the Civil Police confirmed the feminicide investigation. For this record: a documented killing in Bahia framed by the state police as gender-based (feminicide) with the suspect initially released.

adds.title: Bahia é o sétimo estado que mais mata trans, aponta relatório; relembre casos
adds.summary: G1 Bahia, Jan. 27, 2023: the ANTRA dossier ranked Bahia the seventh Brazilian state most killing trans people, with 7 killings of travestis in the state in 2022, and recapped emblematic cases; Pernambuco led that year's negative ranking nationally. For this record: documents Bahia's appearance in the top-ranked band of consecutive annual dossiers, grounding the summary's persistence finding across years.

adds.title: MT ocupa o 12º lugar em assassinato de pessoas trans e travesti
adds.summary: Diario de Cuiabá, Jan. 27, 2026: Mato Grosso ranked 12th among Brazilian states for killings of trans and travesti people in 2025, against a national total of 80, and the state has recorded 43 killings of travestis, trans women, trans men, transmasculine and non-binary people since 2017. For this record: a Mato Grosso-specific reading of the same ANTRA dossier the summary cites for the state's 3 killings in 2025.

adds.title: Empresário é condenado a 13 anos de prisão por morte de mulher trans em MT
adds.summary: G1 MT, Apr. 16, 2026: businessman Jorlan Cristiano Ferreira, 44, was sentenced by a jury to 13 years and 6 months in prison for the feminicide of trans woman Mayla — found dead with knife wounds in January 2024 on a farm beside MT-485 in Sorriso — plus procedural fraud and corpse concealment; the jury held the killing was motivated by gender-based contempt and discrimination. For this record: a documented Mato Grosso conviction that explicitly recognizes the gender dimension of a trans woman's killing.

adds.title: Travestis e transexuais têm direito ao uso do nome social em MT
adds.summary: Diario de Cuiabá, Mar. 16, 2021: a decree published in the state's official gazette on Mar. 12, 2021 guarantees travestis and trans people in Mato Grosso the right to use their social name, accepted by state public offices and usable on badges, cards and identification documents, with state employees able to register the social name in internal records and systems and official publications forbidden from using the civil name without consent. For this record: an identified Mato Grosso state-government measure recognizing trans identity, relevant to documents and name usage within the state.
